relations.subject: sdk:scoped-vs-global-search-indexes
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: predicate reused; object is an unconfirmed candidate id (version:server-7-6) - only server-6-5 and server-7-0 version concepts were visible in the registry at extraction time, so this may need minting or reconciling by the coordinator
relations.evidence: This is because the Search Service supports, as of Couchbase Server 7.6, a new form of "scoped index" in addition to the traditional "global index".

cross_product_finding: The Search Service has no statement-level artifact analogous to SQL++'s CREATE INDEX/GRANT - Search indexes are managed via REST/UI (documented in server/), and this SDK page is purely about querying an index that already exists, using a Search-specific query DSL (`SearchQuery.match()`, `.term()`, etc.) that has no n1ql:* counterpart at all. So there is no reuse candidate in the registry for this page's core concept; it must be entirely SDK-specific vocabulary. This is a useful negative case for the batch's central question: for services without a SQL++ surface, the 'reuse the statement concept' option isn't available even in principle, so the SDK-specific concept family is not a judgment call here so much as the only option.
notable_absence: The relation object 'https://docs.couchbase.com/ld/concepts/version/server-7-6' for the scoped-vs-global-index availability gate could not be confirmed against the version/ registry (only server-6-5 and server-7-0 concept files were visible), so it is left unresolved for the coordinator rather than guessed.
